catalog_quote: - la quantité: à la pénultième les voyelles sont toujours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quantité n'a aucune valeur phonologique. d. Tonologie On peut dire qu'elle est normale, mais plus ou moins réversive en ce sens que le "déplacement" ne s'est effectué que sur le préfixe nominal (qui est haut) dans les groupes prépositionnels avec ó ainsi que, parfois, dans le connectif. Ce qui serait le fait de l'influence du ton de la particule ou du préfixe pronominal.

new_statements.quote: - la quantité : à la pénultième les voyelles sont toujours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quantité n'a aucune valeur phonologique.
new_statements.translation: - quantity: in the penultimate [syllable] the vowels are always pronounced more or less long. This quantity has no phonological value.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (288 pp., byte-identical to the live aequatoria.be asset, HEAD 200 / 43933152 bytes re-checked). Rendered p.72 (= printed p.69) at 150 dpi and read the page scan: under 'Esquisse du parler des Libobi', I. Phonologie, c. Phenomenes vocaliques, the last dash item before 'd. Tonologie' reads exactly '- la quantité : à la pénultième les voyelles sont tou-jours prononcée plus ou moins longues. Cette quanti-té n'a aucune valeur phonologique.' -- verbatim as quoted (only line-break hyphenation differs; the scanned layer has 'pénultiène'). Surrounding section: p.68 gives 7 vowels and the consonant chart; p.69 lists coalescence, elision, progressive vowel harmony, devocalisation, then the quant…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Libobi (a Bamwe variety) the vowel of the penultimate syllable is automatically and non-contrastively lengthened, i.e. a fixed penultimate prominence realised as length; the author does not call it accent or stress, and vowel length is otherwise not phonemic. The language is tonal (two tones H/L, with 'displaced' tonology and a phonetic mid tone).
new_statements.exceptions: None; 'toujours' (always) but 'plus ou moins longues' (more or less long).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain not specified (the statement is in the word-level phonology of the sketch; whether the penult is that of the word or of the phrase/utterance is not said). Stated only in the Libobi sketch (informants from Libulu village, groupement Libobi, zone de Kungu); the Lifonga and Likata sketches of the same 'sous-groupe Bamwe' in the same volume are silent on length and accent, and Donzo 2015 (Libobi, Monyongo) mentions no accent and denies phonological length. Reading 'fixed: penultimate syllable' is an interpretation of automatic penultimate lengthening as the locus of prominence in a tone language, hence low confidence.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Libobi variety (parler des Libóbi: groupement Libobi, zone de Kungu, villages Bolenge, Bosongo, Libulu, Luonga, Boliba; informants from Libulu), which Motingea places in the 'sous-groupe Bamwe' and Glottolog files under bamw1238 (Bamwe has no dialect glottocodes; Glottolog attaches the Libobi, Likata, Lifonga sketches and the Monyongo memoire to bamw1238). Donzo 2015 likewise counts Libobi speakers among the peoples 'generalement appeles bamwe'. The sister sketches of Lifonga and Likata (same volume) make no corresponding statement, so the penultimate-lengthening remark is attested for Libobi only.

tone_statements.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1989. Eléments pour la recherche sur les langues de la Ngiri. In: Africanistique au Zaïre. Actes du premier colloque d'Aequatoria (10-13 octobre 1987) (Études Aequatoria 7), 213-227. Bamanya-Mbandaka: Centre Aequatoria.
tone_statements.quote: La tonologie pourtant, un fait très important. La tonologie nous amenerait en effet, à regrouper les parlers de la Ngiri en 4 grandes subdivisions selon qu'il en existe d'abord à deux et à trois registres et ensuite à tonologie type normal (comparativement au Proto-Bantu) et à tonologie déplacée (réversif). Dans ce dernier cas L.B. De Boeck distingue encore deux sous-types : type Bangála-des-marais et type Dzámba. L'auteur indique que la tonologie Bangála-des-marais a connu un déplacement qui s'est effectué non seulement à l'intérieur du nom, mais a persisté sur l'adjectif qualificatif suivant le nom, sur la construction génitive, etc.
tone_statements.translation: Tonology, however, [is] a very important fact. Tonology would in effect lead us to regroup the Ngiri parlers into 4 large subdivisions, according first to whether there are two or three registers, and then to whether the tonology is of the normal type (compared with Proto-Bantu) or of the displaced (reversive) type. In the latter case L.B. De Boeck further distinguishes two sub-types: the Bangala-des-marais type and the Dzamba type. The author indicates that Bangala-des-marais tonology underwent a displacement that took place not only inside the noun but persisted onto the qualifying adjective following the noun, onto the genitive construction, etc.
tone_statements.locator: p. 220, section 4 'Description des langues', 1. Phonologie; Libinza is listed among the '18 idiomes de la Ngiri' on p. 218; the passage continues p. 221 with Sómbe examples and 'il existe tonétiquement trois régistres' (for Sómbe).
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: GROUP-LEVEL statement only: all Ngiri riverine parlers (Libinza named among them, p. 218) are register-tone languages with either two or three tone registers, of either the 'normal' (Proto-Bantu-like, 'type lingala') or 'displaced/reversive' (Bangala-des-marais, Dzamba) type after De Boeck 1951; the article does not say which subdivision Libinza belongs to and gives no Libinza forms.

sources.note: Nothing on accent/stress. Phonology chapter: seven phonemic vowels; 'La longueur ou quantite vocalique a statut phonologique.. est inexistante dans les langues a l'etude' (pp.44-45), only expressive non-distinctive length; two basic tones H/L plus rising/falling contours (p.62). a full-text search for stress/accent/penultieme/intensite gives no relevant hit.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaire. Elements de structure grammaticale (Etudes Aequatoria 8). Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. 284 pp. [contains the three Glottolog-listed Bamwe sketches: Le parler des Lifonga pp.32-49, Le parler des Likata pp.49-67, Esquisse du parler des Libobi pp.68-88; open PDF at aequatoria.be]
sources.note: Libobi sketch, I. Phonologie c. Phenomenes vocaliques p.69: vowels of the penultimate syllable are always pronounced more or less long, and this quantity has no phonological value (automatic penultimate lengthening; the word 'accent' is not used). Lifonga phonology pp.32-35 and Likata phonology pp.49-50 treat vowels, consonants and tone ('tonologie deplacee', H/L plus a phonetic mid) and say nothing about accent or length. Whole-volume a full-text search for stress/accent/penulti/intensite/quantite: p.69 is the only prosodic-prominence statement in the book.
